sections.overview: The Osprey is a fish-eating raptor found on every continent except Antarctica.
sections.identification: Adults have dark brown upperparts, white underparts and a pale head crossed by a dark eye-stripe.
sections.habitat: It nests near lakes, rivers, lagoons or coasts where fish are accessible; nest sites may be trees or, in Mediterranean populations, cliffs.
sections.diet: Fish make up almost all of its diet, and it catches them by plunging feet-first into the water.
sections.behavior: It is a diurnal hunter and often searches for prey while flying above water or from a perch.
sections.reproduction: A pair generally lays one clutch of one to three eggs each year and may reuse the same nest site.
sections.ecology: Migratory populations move between northern breeding areas and warmer wintering grounds, while some populations are resident.
sections.conservation: The global assessment classifies the species as Least Concern; local populations can nevertheless face disturbance and habitat-specific pressures.
